research.name: Ken Paxton
research.oneLiner: Ken Paxton is the Texas Attorney General and the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas in 2026.
qualifications: Texas Attorney General since 2015; term ends Jan 1, 2027
JD, University of Virginia School of Law, 1991
BA in psychology (1985) and MBA (1986), Baylor University; student body president
Attorney at Strasburger & Price; in-house counsel at J.C. Penney
Ran own McKinney law firm (estate planning, probate, real estate); about 14 years
keyPositions: Lower taxes, less federal spending, and fewer energy regulations
Proposed housing and healthcare tax deductions (July 2026)
Back Trump's tax, border, and deportation priorities
Supports school prayer and Ten Commandments displays in classrooms
Supports parental rights; opposes 'gender ideology' in classrooms
Backs gun rights and abortion restrictions
endorsements: Sen. Ted Cruz campaigned with him
criticisms: Impeached 121–23 by Texas House in 2023 over alleged favors to developer Nate Paul; Senate acquitted
2020: senior aides reported him to FBI for allegedly abusing office to help Paul; he denies it
Tribune/ProPublica: nearly 1,000 trips with $3.3M state security detail since 2015; only 138 tied to state business
Trips included 53 to Florida and 24 to Utah, where a family trust owns properties; 17 during 2023 suspension
Tribune/ProPublica (Sept 2026): disclosures appear to violate federal law, omitting rental income and Utah condo mortgages
Valued Texas land stake at up to $50,000; a partner says it is worth about $1 million
2015 felony securities fraud indictment; resolved by 2024 pretrial diversion, ~$300,000 restitution; dismissed 2025
Has not accepted any of five TV debate invitations, including Fox News
Talarico says he dodged debates and demands repayment of travel costs
Cornyn cited legal troubles, character, corruption, and impeachment during primary
Ex-NAAG head Chris Toth called travel pattern 'ethically and morally problematic'
Dallas Morning News editorial: refuses to share a stage and 'lies about why'

redFlags.title: Impeached by Texas House (2023); acquitted by Senate
redFlags.explanation: The Texas House impeached him 121–23 in May 2023 over alleged bribery-related favors to developer Nate Paul and whistleblower retaliation. The Texas Senate acquitted him on all 16 tried articles on Sept 16, 2023.

redFlags.title: Co-owns cell tower company leasing to Verizon and Dish
redFlags.explanation: His 2025 disclosure valued the stake at $250,000–$500,000 with $100,000–$1 million income, from leases to Verizon and Dish. Telecommunications companies are subject to federal legislation and regulation that senators shape.
